questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code streams and processes a large notification batch? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A client posts a 400 MB request with several million messages. What bounds the handler's memory use?
choices: http.MaxBytesReader, which buffers up to 512 MB so the decoder always sees the complete body.
The json.Decoder reads incrementally and messages are decoded one at a time and flushed in groups of 500, so memory stays roughly constant regardless of body size.
The Publisher, which applies backpressure by blocking the TCP connection.
Nothing: dec.Decode(&m) loads the whole messages array before the loop starts.

questions.prompt: A client sends a body of 600 MB. What does it get back, and what happened to the messages in the first 512 MB?
choices: 400 Bad Request, and nothing was published because the size is validated before processing.
202 Accepted, because the decoder stops reading at the limit and treats it as end of input.
500, and the published messages are rolled back by the Publisher.
413 Request Entity Too Large, and every complete batch read before the limit was hit has already been published.

questions.prompt: A client receives 400 for a malformed message at position 1,200,000 and retries the identical request. What is the main consequence?
choices: The messages published before the malformed entry are published again, since nothing in the handler or publisher deduplicates them.
The retry resumes from message 1,200,000 because the handler remembers progress.
The retry fails immediately because the campaign was already marked as started.
Nothing, because JetStream publishes are idempotent per subject.
